about: E54's chapter cut (the plan's D1 and D2; chapter.mjs is over 1300 lines, so the split applies): "DEATH" (`livingStudents` .. `chooseFirst`) into death.mjs and "THE BODY IS FOUND" (`faintPrepCandidates` .. `openBodyDiscoveryDialog`) into body.mjs; chapter.mjs keeps "CHAPTER END AND THE NEXT SESSION", the re-export of settings.mjs's death predicates and the season registry's two rows. One manifest, two targets: D1 and D2 as one run. Run as windows.json's about says, with this manifest.
facadeNote: E54 (the plan's D1, D2): a death lives in death.mjs and a body found in body.mjs, both re-exported here; this
file keeps the chapter's end and the next session.

header: A body found (E54, the plan's D2): the prep traces promoted (`faintPrepCandidates`, `promoteFaintPrep`), the discovery
and its queue (`discoverBody`, `runDiscovery`), the bodies published (`publishFoundBodies`), the announcement and its
hook (`announceBody`, `BODY_ANNOUNCED_HOOK`, `registerBodyAnnounced`), who finds a body and who saw it
(`openBodyDiscoveryDialog`). Moved out of chapter.mjs, which re-exports every name it exported. Not body-tile.mjs, E63's tile.
A death (E54, the plan's D1): who is alive (`livingStudents`, `livingStudentsForGm`), a death marked, kept secret,
the victim's Truth Bullets (`bulletsHeldBy`, `keepBulletDeletions`, `destroyBullets`), the season's deaths and bodies
cleared and counted, and the death window (`openDeathDialog`, `chooseFirst`). Moved out of chapter.mjs, which
re-exports every name it exported; the predicates stay settings.mjs's (code.md, "Death is two predicates").
targets.statementsWhy: the season registry's row stands in the file of the functions it names (R1254: an entry's clear, tally or keep is a top-level function of its owner's file)

repoint.about: tools/e54/repoint.mjs's part for this cut (sheet.json's `repoint` says what each field is).

sites.why: the card-producing sites per file, as R3510's own classifier counts them on the split tree (13.11.2026); the script holds them to the old row's sums

targetsOrder: body.mjs before death.mjs: R56 cuts openBodyDiscoveryDialog, the last of the body's code, until the next declaration, which stays in chapter.mjs; in the family's text a file is followed by the family's line only when it is not the last, so the body's file may not be last (repoint.mjs refuses otherwise)
